chapters.1.lds: The lesson connects returning to God with becoming holy. Why does the angel question the patrol’s report of peace?
chapters.1.summary: In the second year of Darius, Zechariah calls the people to return to the LORD. Their fathers ignored the prophets, and the warnings came true. Then Zechariah sees a vision at night. A man on a red horse stands among myrtle trees with other riders. They have patrolled the earth and found it quiet. The LORD’s angel asks how long Jerusalem must go without mercy. God answers with kind and comforting words. He is angry with the nations that are at ease.
chapters.2.lds: The lesson studies God dwelling among a people who become holy. How does the promise of protection change the meaning of the measuring line?
chapters.2.summary: Zechariah sees a man with a measuring line going to measure Jerusalem. An angel sends word to stop him. Jerusalem will be like villages without walls, since so many will live there. The LORD will be a wall of fire around it. He calls the exiles to escape from Babylon. Whoever touches them touches the apple of his eye. He is coming to live among his people. Many nations will join themselves to the LORD and be his people.
chapters.3.lds: The lesson uses Joshua’s changed clothing to discuss holiness and changed conduct. What must Joshua still do after receiving clean clothing?
chapters.3.summary: Zechariah sees the high priest Joshua standing before the LORD’s angel. The accuser stands at his right hand. The LORD rebukes the accuser and calls Joshua a stick snatched from the fire. Joshua is wearing filthy clothes. The angel orders them removed and says his guilt is taken away. He is dressed in fine robes and a clean turban. He is told to walk in God’s ways. God promises to bring his servant, the Branch.
chapters.4.lds: Why does the promise mention both laying the foundation and finishing the house?
chapters.4.summary: An angel wakes Zechariah and shows him a gold lampstand with seven lamps. Two olive trees stand beside it. The angel gives a word for Zerubbabel the governor. The work will be done by God’s Spirit, not by might or power. The great mountain before him will become level ground. His hands laid the temple’s foundation, and his hands will finish it. No one should despise the day of small things. The two olive trees are the two anointed ones.
chapters.5.lds: What happens when the curse enters houses built to shelter their owners?
chapters.5.summary: Zechariah sees a huge scroll flying through the air. It carries a curse over the whole land. It condemns everyone who steals and everyone who swears falsely. It will enter their houses and consume timber and stone. Then he sees a measuring basket with a lead cover. A woman sits inside, and she is called Wickedness. Two winged women lift the basket into the sky. They carry it away to the land of Babylon.
chapters.6.lds: How do gifts from distant people become part of the temple’s future?
chapters.6.summary: Zechariah sees four chariots come out between two bronze mountains. They go out to patrol the whole earth. Then God tells him to collect silver and gold from exiles newly come from Babylon. He must make a crown and set it on Joshua the high priest. He says a man called the Branch will build the LORD’s temple. That man will rule on his throne and be a priest there. The crown will be kept in the temple as a reminder. People from far away will come and help build.
chapters.7.lds: The lesson connects holiness with compassion and protection for injured neighbors. Why does the answer move from fasting dates to injured neighbors?
chapters.7.summary: Men come from Bethel to ask the priests a question. For years they have fasted in the fifth month. They ask whether they should continue. God asks whether their fasting was really for him. He recalls what the earlier prophets said. Judge fairly, and show kindness and mercy to one another. Do not oppress widows, orphans, foreigners, or the poor. The fathers refused to listen, and so they were scattered.
chapters.8.lds: The lesson studies truth and peace as part of a future holy community. What do playing children show about the city’s restored life?
chapters.8.summary: The LORD says he is returning to Zion to live in Jerusalem. Old men and women will sit in its streets with their canes. The streets will be full of boys and girls playing. God will bring his people from east and west. He tells them to be strong and finish the temple. They must speak truth and judge fairly at their gates. The fasts will become glad feasts. Ten foreigners will take hold of one Jew’s robe and ask to go with him.
chapters.9.lds: The lesson reads the coming king through Matthew’s later account of Jesus entering Jerusalem. How does removing weapons explain the announced peace?
chapters.9.summary: A message of judgment falls on Syria, Tyre, and the Philistine cities. God will guard his house against every army. Zion is told to rejoice, for her king is coming. He is righteous and humble and rides on a donkey. He will remove chariots, war horses, and bows from Israel. He will speak peace to the nations and rule from sea to sea. God will free the prisoners because of his covenant. He will save his people like a flock.
chapters.10.lds: How does failed guidance leave the people like untended sheep?
chapters.10.summary: The people are told to ask the LORD for rain in the spring. Household idols speak nonsense, and fortune-tellers see lies. Their comfort is empty. So the people wander like sheep with no shepherd. God is angry with the shepherds and will care for his flock himself. He will strengthen Judah and save the house of Joseph. He will whistle for them and gather them in. He will bring them home from Egypt and Assyria.
chapters.11.lds: The lesson connects the weighed silver with Matthew’s later account concerning Judas. What happens when the people responsible for care treat the flock as profit?
chapters.11.summary: Zechariah is told to shepherd a flock marked for slaughter. Its buyers kill the sheep and feel no guilt. Its sellers thank God that they are rich. He takes two staffs, named Favor and Union. He grows weary of the flock, and they detest him. He breaks the staff Favor and asks for his wages. They weigh out thirty pieces of silver, and he throws it to the potter. He breaks the second staff, and a worthless shepherd follows.
chapters.12.lds: The lesson reads the pierced figure through John’s account and later Revelation. Why does rescue for the tents come before honor for the capital?
chapters.12.summary: The LORD will make Jerusalem a cup that makes the nations stagger. All who try to lift that heavy stone will hurt themselves. The clans of Judah will be like fire among sheaves. The LORD will save the tents of Judah first. David’s house and Jerusalem will not be honored above the rest. Then God will pour out a spirit of grace and prayer. They will look on one they pierced and mourn. Every family will mourn by itself.
chapters.13.lds: The lesson connects the struck shepherd with Matthew and the wounds with Restoration scripture. What does the final exchange say about the survivors’ relationship with God?
chapters.13.summary: On that day a fountain will be opened to cleanse sin. God will remove the names of the idols from the land. False prophets will be ashamed and deny their trade. A sword is called against God’s shepherd. The shepherd is struck, and the sheep scatter. Two thirds of the people will perish. The last third will pass through fire and be refined like silver. They will call on God, and he will call them his people.
chapters.14.lds: The lesson uses daily objects to discuss holiness and gives later readings about Christ’s return. How does holiness on cooking pots change the final image of worship?
chapters.14.summary: A day of the LORD is coming when nations will attack Jerusalem. The city will be taken, and half its people exiled. Then the LORD will fight, and his feet will stand on the Mount of Olives. Living water will flow from Jerusalem all year. The LORD will be king over all the earth. Survivors of the nations will come each year to worship him. Even the bells on the horses will be marked as holy. Every cooking pot in Jerusalem will be holy to the LORD.
